title: The Lungs
question: Which lobe is glowing?
lines: Can you name the lobe that's glowing?
These are the lungs, seen from the front.
Which lobe is it?
Facing you, the right lung is on your left.
Only the right lung has a middle lobe.
It's C. The right middle lobe.
Why it matters: a problem here can blur the heart's edge on an X-ray.

title: The Lungs
question: How many lobes does it have?
lines: Your two lungs aren't twins. Here's why.
Watch the glowing lung: the patient's left one.
How many lobes does it have?
The right lung has three lobes.
The left has only two, and it's smaller to make room for the heart.
It's A. Two lobes.
Why it matters: the left lung has a notch shaped around your heart.

title: The Lungs
question: Which tube is glowing?
lines: You breathe through this tube all day. Can you name it?
Look at the tube above the two lungs.
Which tube is glowing?
The esophagus runs just behind it, but that tube carries food.
This one carries air, and it's also called the windpipe.
It's C. The trachea.
Why it matters: C-shaped rings of cartilage keep it open.

title: The Lungs
question: Which lobe is glowing?
lines: One lobe sits low in the patient's right lung. Which one?
We're looking from behind, so the patient's right is on your right.
Which lobe is glowing?
The left lower lobe looks similar, but it's in the other lung.
The right lung's middle lobe is a small wedge at the front.
It's D. The right lower lobe.
Why it matters: most of the lower lobe lies toward your back.
